questions.question: In the carbonate ion (CO₃²⁻), all the C-O bond lengths are equal. This is due to:

options.text: The presence of a double bond between carbon and one oxygen atom.
options.explanation: This is incorrect because the presence of a double bond between carbon and one oxygen would result in unequal bond lengths.

options.text: The negative charge being localized on one oxygen atom.
options.explanation: This is incorrect because localization of the negative charge on one oxygen would not result in equal bond lengths.

options.text: Resonance structures that delocalize the double bond character over all C-O bonds.
options.explanation: This is correct because resonance structures delocalize the double bond character, resulting in equal bond lengths.

options.text: The sp³ hybridisation of the carbon atom.
options.explanation: This is incorrect because sp³ hybridisation would result in a tetrahedral geometry, which is not relevant to the carbonate ion.

questions.explanation: The carbonate ion exhibits resonance. Its structure can be represented by three equivalent resonance structures, where the double bond character is delocalized over all three C-O bonds. This delocalization results in all C-O bonds having partial double bond character and thus equal bond lengths, which are intermediate between a single and a double bond.

The total number of electron domains is 3 (bond pairs) + 2 (lone pairs) = 5. This corresponds to sp³d hybridisation. According to VSEPR theory, to minimize repulsion, the two lone pairs occupy equatorial positions, resulting in a T-shaped molecular geometry.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.explanation: A) In PCl₅, the central phosphorus atom forms five single bonds. It has 5 electron domains, leading to sp³d hybridisation. questions.explanation: VSEPR (Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion) theory is a model used to predict the geometry of individual molecules from the number of electron pairs surrounding their central atoms. CHCl3 has a non-zero dipole moment.

questions.explanation: CCl4 (carbon tetrachloride) has a tetrahedral geometry. Although each C-Cl bond is polar due to the electronegativity difference between carbon and chlorine, the symmetrical arrangement of these four identical polar bonds in a tetrahedral structure causes their individual bond dipoles to cancel each other out, resulting in a net dipole moment of zero. H2O (bent), NH3 (pyramidal), and CHCl3 (tetrahedral but asymmetrical) all have non-zero dipole moments.

questions.explanation: - CH4 (Methane): Tetrahedral geometry, sp3 hybridization, no lone pairs. Ideal bond angle = 109.5°. - NH3 (Ammonia): Pyramidal geometry, sp3 hybridization, one lone pair. The lone pair-bond pair repulsion is stronger than bond pair-bond pair repulsion, compressing the bond angle to approximately 107°. - H2O (Water): Bent (V-shape) geometry, sp3 hybridization, two lone pairs. The two lone pairs exert even greater repulsion, compressing the bond angle further to approximately 104.5°. Therefore, the increasing order of bond angle is H2O (104.5°) < NH3 (107°) < CH4 (109.5°).
